questions.question:

questions.solution:

• Antonym means a word that has the opposite meaning of the given word.
 
• Let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
 
 
• "**Compelled**" **means forced or pressured to do something.(**मजबूर)
 
 
• Example: Her family compelled her to take the job.
 
 
 
• **"Dissuaded" means being discouraged or advised against doing something**.(रोक)
 
 
• Example: He was finally dissuaded to ignore the matter.
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, it can be concluded that the word "dissuaded" is the antonym of "compelled."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

Mr. Khanna is quite ___________(callous) towards the victims of earthquake.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**sympathetic**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us understand the meaning of the given words:
 
 
• The word **"callous" means showing no concern for others' feelings or suffering. (**दूसरों की भावनाओं या पीड़ा के प्रति कोई चिंता नहीं दिखाना।**)**

 
 
• Example: This isn't callous and soulless; it can be rich and exciting.
 
 
 
 
 
• The antonym of "callous" is** "sympathetic (**सहानुभूति**)," which means showing compassion or understanding for others' emotions or experiences.​**
 
 
• Example: He gave me a sympathetic tone.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, Mr. Khanna is described as "quite callous" towards earthquake victims, indicating that he lacks sympathy for them.
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate antonym to fill in the blank would be "sympathetic," as it expresses the opposite meaning of "callous."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 (**rationalistic**) refers to a belief in using reason and logic to understand the world, and is not directly related to the concept of sympathy or callousness. (दुनिया को समझने के लिए कारण और तर्क का उपयोग करने में विश्वास, और सीधे तौर पर सहानुभूति या संवेदनहीनता की अवधारणा से संबंधित नहीं है।)

 
 
• Option 2 (**unsympathetic**) (सहानुभूतिहीन) is a synonym of "callous," and therefore cannot be the correct antonym.
 
• Option 4 (**nondiplomatic**) refers to a lack of tact or diplomacy in one's communication and is not directly related to the concept of sympathy or callousness. (किसी के संचार में चातुर्य या कूटनीति की कमी)

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up and named P, Q, R, S. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

(S1) Newspapers, especially of the popular variety, aim to do two things: to inform and to entertain.

(P) Entertainment may be principally found in the centre pages of the newspaper in some of the feature articles and in some local news stories.

(Q) The principal aim of the short news report on the front pages is to inform.

(R) Most newspapers are published daily, and the news reporters must make sure that they have up-to-the minute news.

(S) In their news reports they will aim to create a sense of immediacy, to convey the impression that they have ‘rushed’ the news to the reader and ‘that the information contained is the very latest.’

(S6) Reporters also wish to create a sense of authenticity, that is, that their news is accurate and genuine.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**P, Q, R, S**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **The paragraph is about the aims and content of newspapers, with a focus on informing and entertaining readers.**
 
• The first sentence (S1) sets the context and purpose of the paragraph.
 
 
• The sentences (P) and (Q) explain how newspapers achieve their aims of informing and entertaining readers.
 
• The sentence (R) provides additional information about the daily publication of newspapers and the need for up-to-date news.
 
• The sentences (S) and (S6) highlight the importance of immediacy and authenticity in news reporting.
 
 
 
• Thus, it can be concluded that the correct chronology of the given sentences would be: PORS.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word from the sentence.

Ready

She was preparing dinner in an organised manner using well-equipped tools while listening to the radio.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Preparing'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Ready' means prepared for an immediate activity or use. (तैयार)
 
• Among the given options, 'Preparing' comes closest to the meaning of 'ready' as it implies a state of readiness or being prepared. (तैयार करना__)
 
• Listening, organised, and equipped don't suggest a state of readiness directly, but rather are associated actions or conditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Option 1'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Preparing: This action implies making something or oneself ready in advance. This is the closest synonym to 'ready' among the options. (तैयार करना)
 
• Listening: This is a verb indicating the action of paying attention to sound or hearing something. It doesn't directly relate to the state or action of being 'ready'. (सुनना)
 
• Organised: Being organized suggests a state of being arranged in a systematic way or being well-structured. While it can contribute to one being ready, it's not a direct synonym. (संगठित)
 
• Equipped: This signifies having the necessary items for a particular purpose. While being equipped can lead one to be ready, the words do not share a synonymous meaning. (सुसज्जित)

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.

B. I am especially proud of it, not only because it has survived several winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.

C. The tree had grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.

D. Last summer, I spent many days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**DCBA**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **The paragraph is about the author's prized peach tree and their observations of it during the summer.**
 
• The correct order of the sentences is:
 
 
• 1.D - mentions the subject of the passage and explains the author's observations of ants on the tree.
 
• 2. C - describes the location and growing conditions of the tree.
 
• 3. B - expresses the author's pride in the tree's survival and productivity.
 
• 4. A - describes the author's observation of the tree's leaves withering during the summer.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct order will be "**DCBA.**"

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Was the bag packed by Mary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Did Mary pack the bag?**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the active voice, the subject of a sentence performs the action.
 
• It follows a clear subject + verb + object construct that's easy to read.
 
 
• Example: The dog chases the cat. 
 
 
 
• **In active voice, the subject of the sentence (Mary) should come before the verb (pack).**
 
• **"Did" is the helping verb used to form the questions or interrogative sentences in past tense.**
 
• The sentence will now reads as a direct question, rather than a passive statement i.e.
 
 
• Did Mary pack the bag?
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4.**
